original_question: In the just-in-time or interval-scheduling problem P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|sum w_j U_j on parallel identical machines, where each job can be processed only on an allowed subset of machines and its processing time equals the length of its release-to-due-date window, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?
target_in_paper: Section 4.4, Open Problem 8: Is P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ w_j U_j fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It identifies the correct open problem, the correct machine environment P (parallel identical machines), the machine-eligibility restriction M_j, the defining condition d_j-r_j=p_j, the weighted tardy-job objective Σ w_j U_j, and the intended parameter m, the number of machines. It also correctly places the problem in the paper's interval-scheduling / just-in-time scheduling context.
missing_details: The paper assumes nonpreemptive processing by default; for a stand-alone formulation this should be stated explicitly.
In the P environment, each job is processed on exactly one of the m identical machines, and each machine can process at most one job at a time.
The meaning of U_j should be made explicit: U_j=0 if job j finishes by its due date d_j, and U_j=1 otherwise.
To make the interval-scheduling interpretation fully explicit, d_j-r_j=p_j means that any on-time execution of job j must occupy its unique interval [r_j,d_j].
The objective may be stated equivalently as maximizing the total weight of just-in-time jobs / scheduled intervals; the paper presents this section as a throughput problem.
Fixed-parameter tractable should be unpacked as asking for an algorithm with running time f(m)·poly(n), where m is the parameter and n is the input size.

For full faithfulness to the paper, it helps to note that the unrestricted problem P|d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ w_j U_j is polynomial-time solvable, while the open question concerns the NP-hard machine-restricted variant P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ w_j U_j.
The paper's notation assumes integer data: p_j, r_j, d_j, and w_j are natural numbers.
If the interval-scheduling wording is used, it should be explicit that each selected job must be assigned to one allowed machine in M_j.
refined_question: Does the machine-restricted just-in-time (equivalently, interval-scheduling) problem P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ_j w_j U_j admit a fixed-parameter algorithm with respect to the number m of parallel identical machines? Concretely: given m identical machines and jobs j with integer weight w_j, processing time p_j, release date r_j, due date d_j satisfying d_j-r_j=p_j, and an eligibility set M_j⊆{1,…,m}, where jobs are processed nonpreemptively on exactly one allowed machine and each machine handles at most one job at a time, can one compute in f(m)·poly(n) time a schedule minimizing Σ_j w_j U_j, where U_j=0 if job j completes by d_j and U_j=1 otherwise?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 4.4 exactly. The paper first introduces interval scheduling / just-in-time scheduling, identifies it with P|d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ w_j U_j, then immediately turns to the machine-restricted variant P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ w_j U_j, states that this variant is NP-hard and solvable in O(n^{m+1}) time, and poses Open Problem 8 asking precisely whether it is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines. The preliminaries provide the meanings of P, M_j, U_j, the default nonpreemptive assumption, and the formal notion of fixed-parameter tractability.
